content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Maccabees Chapter 2

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Translators:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 38

---

## Disagreement Entries

**1MA 2:7 — "Woe to me" vs. "Woe is me"**
- EMET: "Woe to me!"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "Woe is me!" / "Why was I born..."
- RULING: "Woe is me!" — standard biblical idiom in English

**1MA 2:7 — "ruin of my people" vs. "destruction of my people"**
- EMET: "ruin of my people"
- LOGOS: "destruction of my people"
- PNEUMA: expands with "My people are being destroyed"
- RULING: "ruin of my people" — *ptosis* means a falling/ruin, not an active destruction process

**1MA 2:8 — "man without honor" vs. "man stripped of honor"**
- EMET: "a man without honor"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "a man stripped of honor"
- RULING: "a man stripped of honor" — the passive stripping is more contextually accurate; the temple was actively despoiled

**1MA 2:9 — "vessels of her glory" vs. "precious vessels of her glory"**
- EMET: "vessels of her glory"
- LOGOS: "precious vessels of her glory"
- PNEUMA: "treasures" (simplifies)
- RULING: "precious vessels of her glory" — *ta skeuê tês doxês* carries the sense of honored/weighty vessels

**1MA 2:10 — "inherited her palace" vs. "taken its share of her royal precincts"**
- EMET: "inherited her palace and not seized her spoils"
- LOGOS: "taken its share of her royal precincts and seized her spoils"
- PNEUMA: "helped itself to her palace and grabbed its share of the plunder"
- RULING: "taken its portion of her palaces and seized her spoils" — plural *basileia* ("royal things/palaces") is better rendered as plural

**1MA 2:12 — "our holy things, our beauty, and our glory"**
- All translators agree on this triplet. No disagreement.

**1MA 2:14 — "mourned exceedingly" vs. "mourned bitterly" vs. "wept without restraint"**
- EMET: "mourned exceedingly"
- LOGOS: "mourned bitterly"
- PNEUMA: "wept without restraint"
- RULING: "mourned greatly" — the Greek *ependthesen megalos* means mourned greatly; LOGOS's "bitterly" adds a nuance not in the text

**1MA 2:15 — "king's officers who were enforcing the apostasy"**
- All translators agree. No disagreement.

**1MA 2:18 — "friends of the king"**
- All translators preserve "friends of the king" as a technical designation (philoi tou basileos — a court title). No disagreement.

**1MA 2:20 — "Heaven forbid" vs. "God forbid"**
- EMET: "God forbid"
- LOGOS: "Heaven forbid"
- PNEUMA: implied negation in speech
- RULING: "Heaven forbid" — *hileos hemin* is a Greek oath formula; "heaven" is more precise than "God" here

**1MA 2:22 — "to the right hand or to the left"**
- All translators agree on this idiom from Deuteronomy. No disagreement.

**1MA 2:24 — "his kidneys trembled" — visceral emotion**
- EMET: "his kidneys trembled" (very literal)
- LOGOS: "his heart was stirred"
- PNEUMA: "burning in his gut" / "zeal blazed up inside him"
- RULING: "he was moved to his very depths with burning zeal" — the anatomical specificity in Greek (*enetinachthesan hoi nephroi*) is a Hebraism; English needs to convey the visceral depth without the literal organs

**1MA 2:24 — "in righteous indignation" vs. "according to the law"**
- EMET: "according to the law" (kata ton nomon)
- LOGOS: "in righteous indignation"
- PNEUMA: not rendered separately
- RULING: "in righteous indignation" — *kata ton nomon* here means "as was right by the law" but English "righteous indignation" captures the spirit; EMET's reading is technically more literal but misses the evaluative force

**1MA 2:26 — "just as Phinehas did to Zimri son of Salu"**
- EMET: "just as Phinehas did to Zimri son of Salu"
- LOGOS: "just as Phinehas had done against Zimri son of Salu"
- PNEUMA: "the same zeal that Phinehas had shown against Zimri son of Salu"
- RULING: "just as Phinehas had done to Zimri son of Salu" — LOGOS past perfect is correct

**1MA 2:27 — "maintains the covenant" vs. "stands by the covenant"**
- EMET: "maintains the covenant"
- LOGOS: "stands by the covenant"
- PNEUMA: "holds to the covenant"
- RULING: "stands by the covenant" — *histamenos* is "standing" — the posture of defense

**1MA 2:29 — "seeking justice and judgment" vs. "seeking righteousness and justice"**
- EMET: "seeking justice and judgment"
- LOGOS: "seeking righteousness and justice"
- PNEUMA: "hungry for justice and righteousness"
- RULING: "seeking righteousness and justice" — *dikaiosynen kai krima* = righteousness (personal) and justice (social/legal)

**1MA 2:31 — "disregarded the king's command" vs. "rejected the king's command"**
- EMET: "disregarded"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "rejected"
- RULING: "rejected" — *parenoklesan* is stronger than mere disregard; it is active refusal

**1MA 2:33 — "do as the king commands" vs. "do the word of the king"**
- EMET: "do the word of the king"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "do as the king commands"
- RULING: "do as the king commands" — more natural English while preserving the imperial demand

**1MA 2:36 — "did not answer them" vs. "offered no resistance" vs. "made no move to resist"**
- EMET: "did not answer them, nor did they cast a stone"
- LOGOS: "offered no resistance; they threw no stones"
- PNEUMA: "made no move to resist. They did not throw a single stone"
- RULING: LOGOS formulation preserved; EMET's "did not answer them" suggests verbal rather than military response

**1MA 2:37 — "in our innocence" vs. "with a clear conscience"**
- EMET: "in our innocence"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "with a clear conscience"
- RULING: "with a clear conscience" — the Greek *en haploteti* means with simplicity/sincerity; "innocence" is acceptable but "clear conscience" is more accessible

**1MA 2:38 — "about a thousand souls"**
- All translators agree on this figure and the word "souls." No disagreement.

**1MA 2:40 — "from the earth" vs. "off the face of the earth"**
- EMET: "destroy us from the earth"
- LOGOS: "wipe us off the face of the earth"
- PNEUMA: "finish us off quickly. There will be nothing left"
- RULING: "destroy us from the earth" — LOGOS adds "face of the" which is not in the Greek

**1MA 2:41 — "took counsel" vs. "reached this decision" vs. "made a ruling"**
- EMET: "took counsel on that day"
- LOGOS: "came to this decision"
- PNEUMA: "made a ruling"
- RULING: "reached this decision" — the Greek *ebouleusanto* is a deliberate decision reached by counsel

**1MA 2:42 — "congregation of the Hasideans" vs. "group of the Hasideans" vs. "company of the Hasideans"**
- EMET: "congregation of the Hasideans"
- LOGOS: "group of the Hasideans"
- PNEUMA: (same as LOGOS)
- RULING: "a company of the Hasideans" — *synagoge* here refers to an assembly, but "congregation" implies a religious body; "company" fits the military context; "group" is too vague

**1MA 2:44 — "struck sinners in their anger"**
- All translators agree on the structure. Minor word variation in "anger" vs. "fury."
- RULING: "struck down sinners in their anger and lawless men in their wrath"

**1MA 2:46 — "forcibly circumcised"**
- All agree on "forcibly circumcised." This is a remarkable phrase and all translators preserve it accurately. No disagreement.

**1MA 2:48 — "rescued the Torah" vs. "recovered the Torah"**
- EMET: "rescued the Torah"
- LOGOS: "recovered the Torah"
- PNEUMA: "wrested the Torah"
- RULING: "rescued the Torah" — *errusanto* is a rescue/deliverance word; "recovered" is too neutral

**1MA 2:49 — "arrogance and reproach have grown mighty"**
- EMET: "arrogance and reproach have grown mighty"
- LOGOS: "Arrogance and contempt have now grown strong"
- PNEUMA: "Arrogance has triumphed. Contempt has grown powerful"
- RULING: "arrogance and contempt have grown strong" — LOGOS formulation; "reproach" (*oneidismos*) better rendered as "contempt" in this context

**1MA 2:50 — "give your lives for the covenant"**
- All translators agree. No disagreement.

**1MA 2:52 — "found faithful in trial" vs. "found faithful under trial"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "found faithful in trial"
- LOGOS: "found faithful under trial"
- RULING: "found faithful under trial" — "under" better conveys the weight pressing down

**1MA 2:53 — "lord of Egypt" vs. "ruling Egypt"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "became lord of Egypt"
- PNEUMA: "ended up ruling Egypt"
- RULING: "became lord of Egypt" — *archon Aigyptou* is a title

**1MA 2:54 — "because he was exceedingly zealous with zeal"**
- EMET: "exceedingly zealous with zeal" (cognate construction)
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "burning zeal"
- RULING: "for his burning zeal" — the cognate *zelosai zelos* in Greek is a Hebraism; conveying the intensity is more important than reproducing the cognate in English

**1MA 2:55 — "fulfilled the word" vs. "fulfilled his assigned duty" vs. "fulfilled his commission"**
- EMET: "fulfilled the word"
- LOGOS: "fulfilled his assigned duty"
- PNEUMA: "did everything he was commanded"
- RULING: "fulfilled his commission" — captures the official/authoritative nature of Joshua's task

**1MA 2:56 — "bore witness in the congregation" vs. "gave a true report in the assembly"**
- EMET: "bore witness in the congregation"
- LOGOS: "gave a true report in the assembly"
- RULING: "gave his honest testimony in the assembly" — the Caleb allusion is Numbers 13-14; "testimony" captures the formal witnessing

**1MA 2:57 — "because he was merciful" vs. "because he was compassionate"**
- EMET: "because he was merciful"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "because he was compassionate"
- RULING: "because he was compassionate" — *en to eleemoni einai auton* is better rendered as compassionate in this historical summary context

**1MA 2:62 — "his glory will be dung and worms"**
- All translators agree on this striking phrase. No disagreement.

**1MA 2:65 — "a man of counsel" vs. "a man of wise counsel"**
- EMET: "a man of counsel"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "a man of wise counsel"
- RULING: "a man of wise counsel" — *boules* alone is "counsel" but the context of the deathbed commendation implies the counsel is reliable/wise

**1MA 2:66 — "wage the war of the people" vs. "lead the campaign of the people"**
- EMET: "wage the war of the people"
- LOGOS: "lead the campaign of the people"
- PNEUMA: "lead the people's fight"
- RULING: "lead the campaign of the people" — LOGOS preserves the military technical sense of *polemon*

**1MA 2:68 — "render recompense" vs. "pay back" vs. "repay in full"**
- EMET: "render recompense to the nations"
- LOGOS: "pay back the Gentiles what they deserve"
- PNEUMA: "Give the Gentiles what they have coming"
- RULING: "Repay the Gentiles in full" — preserves the justice/proportionality sense of *apodote antapodoma*

**1MA 2:69 — "was added to his fathers" vs. "was gathered to his ancestors"**
- EMET: "was added to his fathers"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "was gathered to his ancestors"
- RULING: "was gathered to his ancestors" — standard biblical death formula; "gathered" reflects the Hebrew *ne'esaf* idiom that the Greek *prosetethê* translates
